intro.title: Responsive typography (clamp)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with text that automatically adjusts its size based on the screen width, using responsive typography. You will learn the core concept of the CSS `clamp()` function, which allows you to set a minimum, preferred, and maximum font size in one line. The main technologies involved are CSS and the `clamp()` function. By the end, you'll understand how to create fluid, readable text that works on both mobile and desktop screens.
intro.usecase: Responsive typography with clamp() is essential for creating fluid text that adapts seamlessly across devices in modern web applications. You'll use this technique in product dashboards where headings and metrics need to scale appropriately from desktop monitors to mobile screens. It's also crucial for marketing websites with hero sections, where taglines must remain readable on all viewports, and in e-commerce product listings where item titles and prices require consistent legibility. This approach eliminates the need for multiple media queries for text sizing, making your CSS more maintainable while ensuring optimal readability across the entire device spectrum.
